title.narrative: Survey and clearance of explosive ordnance contamination in Babella and the neighbouring sub-districts of Maliha and Nashabiyeh

description.narrative: ltpgtExplosive ordnance contamination remains a major protection concern, dangerously affecting the lives and livelihoods of the Syrian population. The widespread explosive contamination continues to threaten lives, hamper access to basic services, and obstruct the delivery of humanitarian assistance and the efforts of the international community towards building resilience and early recovery. United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS)as of January 2024, estimates that since 2013, an average of six people per day have been killed or injured by explosive ordnance. According to the 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), no comprehensive and nationwide survey has been conducted to determine the extent of the explosive ordnance contamination. ltbrgtMine action response activities are key enablers to the delivery of humanitarian aid, services, and early recovery to assist people in need, as well as a prerequisite to safe, dignified and voluntary return. Mine action is a comprehensive approach which requires sustained and flexible funding and mine action mainstreaming supports planning of all sectors through provision of contamination data and enables safe activities by promoting life-saving behaviors through risk education, mitigating and removing threats by survey and clearance. Yet, while delivery of explosive ordnance risk education and awareness messages is widespread, survey and clearance remain geographically limited and underfunded.ltbrgtThrough this project, NPA will deploy local non-technical survey (NTS), technical survey (TS) and clearance teams within the Babella Sub-District of Rural Damascus. They will conduct a comprehensive contamination survey, clearance, and provide a rapid response to explosive ordnance call-out capability. The proposed project will ensure that the entire Babella sub-district is surveyed within the proposed project duration.ltbrgtThe project activities will directly support Strategic Priority 1 within the Syrian Humanitarian Fund First Standard Allocation 2024 – “Support and strengthen the delivery of critical basic services to ensure the most vulnerable populations in under-served locations affected by conflict, displacement, and natural shocks, receive integrated life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian aid”, and the Mine Action Area Of Responsibility (AOR) priority of “survey and clearance to support safe delivery of aid and enhance access to services”.ltbrgtAdditionally, the response will also contribute towards the priority sector - Protection - by minimizing the impact of explosive ordnance for communities most at-risk. It is important to note that the proposed project activities will be able to support UN agencies, INGO and NNGOs in the event that they were to face explosive ordnance contamination during project planning and implementation, which would pose a threat to staff, and delay planned activities. In addition, the project will integrate a referral protocol for services beyond the scope of this project, via the deployment of a NTS team and a dedicated community liaison capacity, to other humanitarian actors operating within Babella, in areas of Gender Based Violence, education, Housing / Land / Property and Water / Sanitation / Health. The referral process will be via email and phone communications between NPA and the relevant humanitarian actors.ltbrgtNPA adheres to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence in its mine action programming and firmly believes in the need to assess and monitor activities to ensure that they contribute positively to social unity and cohesion and do not contribute to further conflict – the ‘Do No Harm’ principle.ltbrgtlt/pgt
